Subject: SOC 2 scope question — dedicated pools vs private VPC

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is finalizing the SOC 2 intake and we need confirmation on scope for your Type II report. Two questions we couldn't confirm from the docs: 1) If a customer is on a Redwood Dedicated pool (tenant-dedicated GPU capacity), is that hosting mode automatically in-scope for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II? 2) If a customer uses a private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC with on-prem option), does that fall outside Redwood's SOC 2 boundary and instead require our own controls?

We plan to include Redwood in our vendor assessment for the Crestview trading platform and need to know if we should request a bridge letter or additional evidence for the dedicated pools. Ideally we'd have clear wording (one-liner) to include in our vendor report.

Can you also confirm the audit period covered by your last Type II report and whether the dedicated-pool bridge letter would cover the same period or a different window?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — security review is on a tight schedule.

Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question — dedicated pools vs private VPC

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: Dedicated pools are generally included in Redwood's SOC 2 Type II when the customer is using Redwood-managed dedicated capacity (we consider tenant isolation, access controls, and the underlying operational controls in-scope). Private VPC / on-prem deployments are typically outside Redwood's SOC 2 scope because the customer controls infrastructure and network; in those cases, Redwood provides a set of control responsibilities and an attestation template for customers to include in their own assessments.

Details and next steps:
- Audit period: Our most recent Type II report covers 2024-07-01 through 2025-06-30 (file: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_202407-202506.pdf).
- Dedicated pools: We provide a bridge letter specifically for customers in managed dedicated pools that documents applicable controls and any exceptions (see attached bridge-letter-dedicated-pools-20270510.pdf). That bridge letter calls out the same audit window by default; if you need coverage for a different window (e.g., a later sampling period or a custom audit request) let us know and we can escalate to compliance for a scoped addendum.
- Private VPC / on-prem: Out of scope for Redwood's SOC 2. We supply a responsibility matrix and sample evidence (network diagrams, configuration templates) to make customer's own audits straightforward.
- Evidence we can provide for vendor assessments: SOC 2 Type II PDF, bridge letter for dedicated pools, tenant isolation diagram, support/access logs extract (on request under NDA).

I'll loop in Laura from Compliance to confirm the bridge letter language and to attach the SOC 2 PDF.

Best,

Hi Asha / team — adding a few compliance specifics to make your vendor report language precise. Please feel free to copy/paste from the block below: 

"Redwood Inference's SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30) covers Redwood-managed hosted and dedicated service operations. For customers on Redwood Dedicated (dedicated GPU pools managed by Redwood), the controls exercised by Redwood over physical/logical isolation, change management, and operational monitoring are included in the SOC 2 scope. Customers that deploy Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC or on-premise installations) are outside Redwood's SOC 2 boundary; Redwood provides a responsibility matrix and templates to support the customer's own audit. A dedicated-pool bridge letter is available to attest to the applicability of controls for dedicated deployments during the stated audit period or a mutually agreed alternate period."

Requested evidence we can provide immediately (PDFs / diagrams): SOC 2 Type II report (full PDF), dedicated-pool bridge letter (customizable to customer name), deployment isolation diagram (high-level), and list of control owners. If Crestview requires log extracts or environment-specific configs, we'll need a signed NDA and an evidence request form so we can scope that work.

Happy to jump on a quick call if you'd like us to walk through the language with your audit team.

Regards,

Hi Asha — one operational note on dedicated pools that might impact your vendor controls: if your workloads use Dedicated with "burst" enabled (reserved pool plus short-term burst into shared capacity), the bridge letter will document the conditions under which burst occurs and how we maintain tenant isolation during those events. For customers who require zero-shared-execution guarantees, we recommend a Reserved Dedicated contract (no burst) or Private deployment.

If you want, we can produce a short one-page statement specific to Crestview that references the report + bridge letter and includes the exact audit window for your vendor file. Please confirm whether you need: (a) the standard bridge letter that aligns to the 2024-07-01 -> 2025-06-30 report, or (b) a customized attestation for a different audit window. If (b), share the dates and we'll route to Compliance for review.
